title: Object Property Editor Adapter

oracle.positive: Edit color/name/property through document command once; undo restores previous value
oracle.negative: Editing derived read-only BRep field must be disabled

reviewer.role: project owner (human reviewer) at the running application

checks_run: RED: none behavioural (the module is new); stated as API-level. F1/F2 hold the negative oracle.
GREEN: cargo test -p om9-app --test property_editor_adapter -> test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
cargo test -p om9-core -p om9-app -j 2: every group passes except the pre-existing, unrelated chrome_actions::icons_scale_with_the_screen_size.
cargo fmt --check: exit 0; cargo clippy -p om9-core -p om9-app --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0

Rename: cargo test -p om9-app --test property_editor_adapter -> 3 passed (E5: one command, journal +1, Undo restores the old name; F1: an empty/padded label is refused with Invalid and writes nothing; F2: Geometry remains read-only).

App adapter: MatrixApp::edit_selected_property(edit) turns one field edit of the single selected object into one document command (it refuses with no single selection), plus MatrixApp::undo_len(). cargo test -p om9-app --test property_editor_adapter -> 4 passed (the new case proves the refusal and the single Undo step).

UI panel: the property editor lives in the Edit menu popup. For the single selected object it offers six items (Visible/Hidden/Selectable/Locked toggles with their state in the label, Colour: red, Colour: layer) and each click goes through MatrixApp::edit_selected_property, so one toggle is one transaction. cargo test -p om9-app --test property_menu_ui -> 1 passed: click Edit, click 'Locked: off', the Undo journal grows by exactly one. This also proves that a menu-popup item click is delivered, which the Super Select attempt of round 26-28 did not demonstrate (that test selected nothing, most likely because its fixture's gem payload is not what the Gems filter classifies as a gem).

Integrity audit (round 34): the new tools/audit_m01_l2_03_14.py checks that every file the eight records cite is on disk (design api.md + crosswalk, both fixtures, the ui-review, every artefact it names, and a ledger entry) and reports: integrity: 0 problem(s) across 8 L3. Output saved as implementation/evidence/M01/OM9-L2-03-14/INTEGRITY_AUDIT.log.
code_change: crates/om9-app/src/session/properties.rs (new): FIELDS table, PropertyField/FieldState, PropertyEdit (editable fields only) and Controller::edit_object_property (one transaction for all edited objects).

crates/om9-core/src/transaction.rs: Mutation::Label { source, label } with its validation, its apply (attributes_revision bump + dependents invalidation) and its source() arm; crates/om9-app/src/session/properties.rs: PropertyEdit::Label and the FIELDS Name row is editable.
crates/om9-app/src/ui/chrome.rs: the Edit menu carries the property editor items (six, one per editable field: the four toggles, two colour presets).

manual_reviewer_checklist.scope_note: The edit path is machine-proven; the panel that shows the fields is the next UI slice.

items.step: Change the colour of a selected object.
items.machine_proven: E1: one journal entry, and Undo restores the previous colour.
items.human_must_verify: The object changes colour at once and one Undo returns the old colour.

items.step: Hide the object through the editor, then Undo.
items.human_must_verify: One Undo brings the object back.

items.step: Look at the field list: which are editable, which are greyed out and why.
items.machine_proven: E3/F2: six editable fields (Name, Color, Visible, Hidden, Selectable, Locked); Geometry is disabled with its reason.
items.human_must_verify: Rename a row and confirm one Undo brings the old name back; confirm Geometry cannot be typed into.

items.step: Try to edit an object whose layer is locked.
items.machine_proven: F3/F4: refused with Permission, no journal entry, value unchanged.
items.human_must_verify: The editor explains the refusal instead of silently doing nothing.
